text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe presents campaign platform including plans to cut taxes and possibly freeze government spending for a five-year period.
-- Socialist Francois Hollande calls for cuts in mandatory contributions, and notably in value-added tax, to boost economic growth.
-- Eurotunnel posts a six-billion-franc net loss for 1996, due to heavy indebtedness. Calls shareholders for July 10 to approve debt restructuring plan.
-- Industrial production rose 1.6 percent in February due to pickup in automobile sector production, linked to exports.
-- A pilots' strike at Air France Europe to cut flights by half today.
LA TRIBUNE

-- Socialist party national secretary Pierre Moscovici says in an interview the Socialists are ready to oppose Germany on European single currency : if elected, they would renegotiate terms of the shift to the single currency, re-evaluate deficit criteria, refuse to exclude Italy from the first wave of countries joining the euro, and call for a European economic government to co-ordinate economic policies.
-- Opinion poll forecasting a narrow lead for the ruling coalition in the upcoming parliamentary election hits stock prices.
-- Eramet open to negotiate transfer of nickel mining fields in New Caledonia.
L'AGEFI
-- Eurotunnel board considers debt for equity swap which would turn bankers into shareholders.
-- Bank of France posts a 1.2 billion francs profit for 1996, down 11.5 percent from 1995.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Air France group expects a 500-million francs profit for year to end March 1998, Air France has not registered a profit since 1990.
-- A Chinese group from Singapore bought around one percent of Paribas, considers increasing stake to three percent.
-- Banque Hervet to be privatised and listed on the Second Marche.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Real-estate sales picked up in Paris from end 1996.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Eurotunnel seeks debt-plan approval as losses narrow.
